fixes.explanation: Yes, baker. The LORD instructs Gad, David's seer, to go and tell David, and the message is, "I am offering you three options. Choose one of them, and I will carry it out against you." (1 Chronicles 21:10). David has to pick one. The three are three years of famine, three months of being swept away before his enemies, or three days of the sword of the LORD (1 Chronicles 21:12).

Yes. Ornan says, "Take it! May my lord the king do whatever seems good to him." (1 Chronicles 21:23). Then he offers the oxen, the sledges and the wheat, saying, "…I will give it all." David won't take it for free, though, and says he insists on paying the full price (1 Chronicles 21:24).

The text gives the sons a different action. It says that "…his four sons who were with him hid themselves." (1 Chronicles 21:20). Telling the king isn't part of that verse. Then David comes to Ornan, and Ornan bows facedown before David (1 Chronicles 21:21).
